podcast.title: Temporary Drummer for Billy Talent
podcast.body: Jordan Hastings was approached by Billy Talent and agreed to learn and record drums for their new album after their regular drummer, Aaron Solowoniuk, needed to step away due to an MS relapse. "But we have reached out to Jordan Hastings from Alexis Amphire. Say yes. Ask if he would have time to come in and learn these songs and record these songs. He has said yes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Aaron Solowoniuk's MS Relapse and Album Absence (2016)
xref.body: On January 15, 2016, Aaron announced on YouTube that he was experiencing an MS relapse, which had been slowing him down for six to seven months. The symptoms made it difficult to perform daily tasks and play drums. He decided to step away from recording drums for the "Afraid of Heights" album to focus on his health, as he was unsure how long his recovery would take. The band fully supported his decision and brought in Jordan Hastings as a fill-in drummer.

xref.title: Band Support for Aaron Solowoniuk and FUMS (2016)
xref.body: Billy Talent, their management, and their record label (Warner Music Canada) are 100% supportive of Aaron in his struggle with MS. They established a charity called FUMS (Fuck U MS) to raise money for MS research. At a music festival on May 29, 2016, a band member (Ben Kowalewicz) addressed the crowd, expressing the band's love, care, and commitment to Aaron, and thanking Jordan Hastings for filling in. The speaker referred to Aaron as "Mr. A. S. Lua," which appears to be a mis-transcription of his full name, Aaron Solowoniuk.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unforeseen Rock am Ring Show (2016)
xref.body: During a Rock am Ring Festival performance in 2016, bad weather and lightning strikes led to the evacuation of the grounds. The band was initially told they wouldn't play, with headliners Deftones and Red Hot Chili Peppers scheduled before them. Unexpectedly, the Red Hot Chili Peppers requested that Billy Talent go on after them, resulting in Billy Talent headlining. The next day, the festival was canceled due to weather. This was Jordan Hastings' third show with the band, with his first two having been in Russia.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fill-in Drummer for Billy Talent
xref.body: Jordan Hastings, a drummer from the band AlexisOnFire, temporarily joined Billy Talent to record drums for the "Afraid of Heights" album and to perform live when Aaron Solowoniuk had to step away due to an MS relapse. He was highly praised for his skill and contribution. His first two shows with Billy Talent were in Russia, and his third was at the Rock am Ring Festival in Germany.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Activities During Hiatus
xref.body: During the band's break, Dallas Green focused on City and Colour; George Pettit became a firefighter; Wade McNeil worked as a radio DJ and in other bands; Jordan Hastings played with Billy Talent; and Chris Steele undertook an expedition to the Himalayas. "Dallas Green focused on City and Colour; George Pettit became a firefighter; Wade McNeil worked as a radio DJ."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Lives
xref.body: Following the band's breakup, members pursued different paths: Dallas Green continued with City and Colour, George Pettit became a firefighter, Wade McNeil became a radio DJ, Jordan Hastings became a fill-in drummer for Billy Talent and played in other bands, and Chris Steele was last heard to have gone for a "truck on the Himalayas." "I mean, Dallas Green is off doing a city and color thing. Vocalist George Pettit became a firefighter. Wade McNeil is doing a bunch of stuff, including working as a radio DJ. Drummer Jordan Hastings is filling it with Billy Talbot and playing in some other bands. And I'm not even sure where bass player Chris Steele is."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
